content: 1. Norgestimate and Norgestrel: Cobicistat increases the levels of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential adverse effects. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate systemic concentrations of norgestrel, increasing the risk of side effects. Consider alternative therapies if available. Atazanavir also increases norgestrel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Nortriptyline: Atazanavir increases nortriptyline levels through an unspecified mechanism. Cobicistat also elevates nortriptyline levels. Use caution, monitor closely, and titrate the antidepressant dose carefully to achieve the desired effect. Start with the lowest feasible dose and adjust as needed during coadministration. 3. Olaparib: Both cobicistat and atazanavir increase olaparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 200 mg (capsule) or 150 mg (tablet) twice daily with moderate CYP3A inhibitors, and to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) twice daily with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 4. Oliceridine: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration is necessary, reduce oliceridine dosing frequency and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. Adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dose to maintain stable drug effects. 5. Omaveloxolone: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. 6. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir (and Dasabuvir): Cobicistat increases the levels of this combination therapy via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. Atazanavir increases paritaprevir levels when coadministered. Modify therapy by administering atazanavir 300 mg (without ritonavir) in the morning with Viekira Pak. 7. Omeprazole: Omeprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing atazanavir solubility and plasma concentrations. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, limit the PPI dose to omeprazole 20 mg and administer ~12 hours before atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naive patients. PPIs are not recommended in treatment-experienced patients taking atazanavir. 8. Ondansetron: Atazanavir and cobicistat increase ondansetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as CYP450 inhibitors may reduce ondansetron clearance. 9. Orlistat: Orlistat decreases atazanavir levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Loss of virological control has been reported in HIV-infected patients taking orlistat concomitantly. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and if an increased viral load is confirmed, discontinue orlistat. 10. Osilodrostat: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase osilodrostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Osimertinib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase osimertinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If no alternatives exist, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 12. Ospemifene: Atazanavir and cobicistat increase ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine decreases atazanavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use caution and monitor closely. Oxcarbazepine decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Consider alternative anticonvulsant or antiretroviral therapy to avoid potential changes in drug exposure. 14. Oxybutynin: Atazanavir increases oxybutynin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 15. Oxycodone: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase oxycodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the oxycodone dose to mitigate the risk of toxicity. 16. Ozanimod: Cobicistat increases ozanimod toxicity by inhibiting BCRP transporters, leading to increased exposure to active metabolites. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 17. Paclitaxel: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase paclitaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 18. Pacritinib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase pacritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 19. Palbociclib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase palbociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 20. Palovarotene: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase palovarotene levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Panobinostat: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase panobinostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the starting dose of panobinostat to 10 mg if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Pantoprazole: Pantoprazole decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing atazanavir solubility and plasma concentrations. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 23. Paricalcitol: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase paricalcitol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 24. Paroxetine: Cobicistat increases paroxetine levels. Use caution, monitor closely, and titrate the antidepressant dose carefully to achieve the desired effect. 25. Pazopanib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 26. Pexidartinib: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase pexidartinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. 27. Penbutolol: Atazanavir increases penbutolol effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely for hypotension, bradycardia, AV block, and prolonged PR interval. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 28. Pentobarbital: Pentobarbital decreases atazanavir levels via CYP3A4 induction. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 29. Perampanel: Cobicistat and atazanavir increase perampanel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 30. Perphenazine: Cobicistat increases perphenazine levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. A dose reduction of antipsychotics metabolized by CYP3A or CYP2D6 may be necessary.
